transcript.text: AEG IKB64301FB induction hob keeps beeping and showing Er03 then switches off. Pan of pasta boiled over just before.

I can't confirm exactly what Er03 means on your AEG hob, so I won't guess at the code. The timing tells us a lot, though. Touch-control hobs are built to beep and switch themselves off if liquid or a wet pan sits on the controls. They treat it as buttons being held down, as a safety measure. A pasta boil-over is a classic way to set that off, because starchy water spreads across the glass and dries into a sticky film. Most likely causes, in order:
1. Water or starchy residue on or near the touch controls. This is very common and easy to fix.
2. Moisture that has seeped under the glass edge or into the electronics. This usually clears once it has dried out.
3. Less likely, a coincidental overheating or control fault. Checks to try:
1. Switch the hob off at its wall switch (the fused spur) or the consumer unit. Let it cool. Hobs are usually wired in rather than plugged in.
2. Wipe the whole glass with a damp cloth, then dry it completely. Pay most attention to the touch-control area and around the edges of the glass. Dried starch can still set off the controls, so clean it off properly. Also take any pans, utensils or cloths off the controls, and dry the base of the pan.
3. Switch it back on and try a zone. If the error has gone, it was liquid on the controls and there is no fault.
4. If the error comes straight back with clean, dry glass, water may have got underneath. Leave it switched off at the spur for several hours, ideally overnight, then try again. If it still shows Er03 after a good dry-out, it's worth having an engineer look at it. That points to the control panel or electronics, which isn't owner work on an induction hob. Call an engineer sooner, and don't keep using the hob, if it trips the electrics, you smell burning or hot plastic, or the glass is cracked. In those cases, leave it isolated at the spur.

Tried it. There was starchy water across the slider and a wooden spoon resting on the edge. I wiped it dry, moved the spoon and switched it off at the wall for 5 minutes. It works now and all four zones are fine. No cracks or burning smell.

That's sorted, then. The starchy water across the slider and the spoon on the edge were enough to make the hob think buttons were being held down. It beeped and shut itself off as a safety measure, which is exactly what it's designed to do. All four zones working, with no cracks and no burning smell, means there's no fault and nothing needs replacing. To stop it happening again:
1. Keep spoons, lids and tea towels off the control strip.
2. Use a bigger pan for pasta, or turn the heat down a notch once it's boiling. A wooden spoon laid across the top of the pan also helps stop it frothing over.
3. If it does boil over, wipe the controls straight away before the starch dries. If Er03 ever comes back when the glass is clean and dry, that would be worth looking into. For now, is there anything else I can help with?

candidates: Liquid or starchy residue from the boil-over sitting on the touch controls, triggering the safety shut-off (high)
Moisture that has got under the glass or into the hob's electronics from the spill (medium)
Overheating protection or a control board fault unrelated to the spill (low)

reading.symptom: keeps beeping, shows error and switches off

plan: Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make AEG; model IKB64301FB; code ER03.
The fault they reported is: "keeps beeping, shows error and switches off". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.

candidates: Starchy water and a wooden spoon on the touch controls triggering the hob's safety cut-out (high)

reading.symptom: hob beeped and switched off showing Er03 after pasta boil-over

plan: The customer says it is fixed: say so warmly, give one short tip to stop it happening again, and ask if there is anything else.
